report.source_text: He was taken to the operating room for an exploratory laparotomy where he was found to have a small bowel mass approximately 30 cm from the ileocecal valve, serving as the lead point for his intussusception. There was also a small palpable lymph node in the associated mesentery. Approximately 15 cm of small bowel and 13 lymph nodes, including the palpable lymph node, were resected and sent for pathological analysis. No abnormalities were seen on the liver.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ileo-ileal intussusception secondary to a T3N1 NET, grade 1
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man presented with lower abdominal pain, maroon colored bowel movements, and hematemesis. Vital signs were stable. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis revealed ileo-ileal intussusception and an irregular area of mucosal/submucosal thickening suspicious for a small bowel mass. He underwent exploratory laparotomy, which confirmed a small bowel mass approximately 30 cm from the ileocecal valve causing the intussusception, with a palpable mesenteric lymph node. Resection of the affected small bowel and lymph nodes was performed. Histopathological examination confirmed a well-differentiated 1.2-cm Neuroendocrine Tumor (NET) with spread to 1 lymph node (N1) and a Ki-67 index of less than 1% (Grade 1), with clear surgical margins. The final diagnosis included T3 staging. His postoperative course was complicated by a resolved ileus.

Exploratory laparotomy revealed a small bowel mass causing intussusception, approximately 30 cm from the ileocecal valve, with a palpable lymph node in the mesentery. Resection of 15 cm of small bowel and 13 lymph nodes was performed.

Histopathological examination confirmed a well-differentiated 1.2-cm NET with spread to 1 lymph node (N1), with surgical margins clear of the tumor. The Ki-67 stain was positive for less than 1% of cells (Grade 1).
The final diagnosis included T3 staging for the NET.
Postoperative course was complicated by the development of an ileus, which quickly resolved on its own following conservative management.
